draftText: Big Walk used AI on well under zero point one percent of its code. If it's your game of the year, this matters, because 19 IGF jurors won't vote for any game using generative AI. Here's the odd part. A chatbot came in after even a Unity engineer got stuck on a slowdown bug. House House now calls having no AI policy a failure. Fair enough, code is creative work too. Still, this is a bug fix, not a scandal. If I had a vote, it'd still get mine. Does Big Walk still get your vote, yes or no?

issues.problem: The sub-0.1% figure is House House's own estimate ('we'd estimate'), but the script states it flatly as fact. The title and description attribute it correctly; the spoken line should too, e.g. 'House House estimates...'.

check.summary: All factual claims are supported by the sources: the jurors' pledge, the Unity engineer and slowdown-bug chatbot fix, the last-resort framing, and the 'failure' quote about having no AI policy. The opinion lines are clearly framed as the narrator's take. The only issue is minor: the spoken script does not attribute the 0.1% figure as the studio's own estimate.
